A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DarkIR work, with 17 readable pages covering the main paper, supplementary material and references. Text, equations, tables and figures support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original DarkIR benchmark results, qualitative restorations and ablation experiments in the main paper and supplementary material.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark evaluations and the supplementary loss-function and feature-propagation ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same Fourier-based encoder, dilated spatial-attention decoder, loss functions and model variants. The supplementary feature-propagation design is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain LOLBlur, Real-LOLBlur, LOLv2-Real/Synthetic and LSRW coverage, the supplementary RealBlur-Night examples, and evaluations on DICM, LIME, MEF, NPE and VV.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding tables and qualitative comparisons. This includes the end-to-end models, two-step enhancement/deblurring pipelines, and supplementary Table C comparators such as CIDNet.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, preprocessing, metrics, model sizes and training settings are identical. Both retain the 10,200/1,800 LOLBlur split, 384-pixel training crops and the stated 256-pixel crops for the block ablations.

E4.justification: Tables 6–8 retain the block, spatial-attention and channel-scaling ablations. Supplementary Tables A–B retain the loss and feature-propagation studies, and all qualitative examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged throughout the main paper and supplement.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–8 and supplementary Tables A–C match. For example, Table 1 retains LOLBlur PSNR values of 27.00 dB for DarkIR-m and 27.30 dB for DarkIR-l. Qualitative results also match.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 retain the same image-formation model, block formulations, losses and feature-propagation expression. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about joint low-light restoration, spatial/frequency attention, computational efficiency, state-of-the-art performance and real-world generalization.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations are unchanged, including the multi-task performance tradeoff on LOLBlur. Section 5 retains the limitation that fewer operations through depth-wise convolutions do not proportionally reduce GPU inference time.

D1.justification: Supplementary implementation details remain identical, including PyTorch, AdamW settings, learning-rate schedule, batch size 32, H100 hardware and augmentations. The code and metric-library links are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 74 reference entries and related-work discussion are retained. Positioning relative to LEDNet, NAFNet, Metaformer and other restoration approaches is unchanged.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v2, dated 31 Jan 2025, to v3, dated 14 Oct 2025, and gains a hyperlink. The paper's wording, headings and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and A–G, and Tables 1–8 and A–C, retain their content, captions, structure and placement. Embedded images are identical; negligible rendering shifts do not alter the layout.

improvement.justification: The main paper and supplement retain identical scientific content, numerical results and qualitative evidence, with the same explanations, reproducibility information and limitations. The updated arXiv stamp and negligible typesetting differences provide no meaningful improvement or deterioration in overall quality.
